utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can we call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor verse Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. On this Wednesday, the 12th of March, 2008, I bid good morning to members of the Prosecution, the witness, Mr. Seselj, and all the people assisting us. We need to continue the hearing with the cross-examination. Before that I should like to tell Mr. Seselj that the Appeals Chamber rendered its decision regarding the appeal which we certified regarding an oral decision that we rendered concerning the coming of a witness. Concerning this issue, the Chamber did not grant the motion of the accused and rejected it, and in accordance with this jurisprudence the Prosecution can call witnesses concerning the municipalities which were suppressed, eliminated, from the indictment, and that is Brcko and Bijeljina. So, Mr. Seselj, you will have the ruling of the Appeals Chamber which will be quickly translated, but I just wish to inform you about it. Therefore, we can now start with the cross-examination, Mr. Seselj, and I give you the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karlovic, what kind of education do you have?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Secondary education.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What school did you graduate from?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The school of transportation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what is your rank?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain, captain with -- four-star captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What other ranks in your case? Let me see. Lieutenant, captain, captain first class, and you said you were a satnik?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is a captain first class, which means four-star captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You retired very young. Why?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't need to tell you what my medical problems are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. I won't go into that, then. You achieved a relatively high rank in view of the fact that you only have secondary school education and no military school, which means that you achieved your rank through military struggle, that you performed very well during the war?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but subsequently I went to a military school.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you didn't go to military academy.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I simultaneously went to a civilian university.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please try and make breaks between questions and answers because the interpreters are having difficulty following.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm asking you about your educational background. For you to be able to answer the question, what does a cockade mean in your view?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know about a cockade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but before answering the question regarding the cockade, I must go back to your educational background. I noted that you were captain first class. You didn't do your military service in the JNA, nor did you go to any military schools, and I thought to myself that you had a rather extraordinary career and made a lot of progress in the Croatian army. Yesterday you told us that you were received by President Tudjman in those days. This morning I wondered whether there may be a cause-and-result relationship. Could you tell me whether in the Croatian army you can become a captain without going through an officer's school of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I wasn't received by the president, Dr. Franjo Tudjman; I was received by his bureau, his office. I was received by one of the people in his office and I made my statement about the events at Ovcara there. Secondly, in the Croatian army it was possible to acquire such a rank. I performed from the lowest functions to the level of battalion commander at the end of my career, and simultaneously we were trained in schools and ranks depending on the duties we performed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I've already asked you what, in your opinion, does the expression a "cockade" mean?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A cockade for me is a Serbian mark or coat of arms used on Serb caps, on the sajkaca and subara caps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why does it have to be a Serbian sign? How would we call the French coat of arms on a French officer's cap?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer that. I can't understand what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How do you Croats today call the metal marking on an officer's hat, or a policeman, or a railwayman's, a postman's cap? How do you call the insignia, the metal mark, the metal badge?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We call it a coat of arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you don't have any special name for this?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the Serbian language a cockade is every insignia worn on a cap, any kind of marking worn on a cap is called a cockade. However, in communist times this was replaced by the expression "five-cornered star." Do you remember? You're a young man, but you remember the communist era. It was called a five-cornered star that was worn on a military cap. Nobody called it a cockade. But in the dictionary of the Serbian language, the only expression that exists for a badge worn on a military cap is a cockade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I'm sorry for interrupting you because now you have been testifying. Will you please ask him the question: If I tell you in Serbia the expression "cockade" means this; do you agree with me or not. If you don't do that, it is you who is testifying, and then the Prosecutor is going to get on his feet and make objections, and we'll be wasting time. So let's be efficient on both sides.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say in Serbia that the sign is called a cockade but in the Serbian language, and I was just going to ask my next question when you interrupted me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you say a cockade, does that always have to mean a Chetnik cockade?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that I had never seen anywhere this badge, nor am I familiar with the Serbian language to know whether this means a badge or coat of arms. As a young man I saw this worn by Chetniks in films and after that I saw it during the war. So I can't discuss what the Serbian word means.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That is not my question. My question is: In your opinion, when the word "cockade" is used, just the word "cockade," does that necessarily have to associate -- be associated with the Chetniks or is it a broader concept? Is a cockade always something belonging to Chetniks? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me, on the basis of my knowledge, a cockade is always Chetnik cockade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And have you -- did you ever come across at the Vukovar theatre of operations and elsewhere, did you come across different types of cockades?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Vukovar I did. Afterwards I didn't see any cockades as I know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Would you describe what you call a cockade?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me a cockade is a metal badge containing a Serbian coat of arms, combined with the traditional caps sajkaca and subara.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So a metal Serbian coat of arms combined with these caps, traditional caps. That's the cockade. And nothing beyond that?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. Would you agree with me when I say that you are not very well versed with a cockade?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree. I'm just telling you what I think about it, but you perhaps know more.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you be kind enough, please, to place on the ELMO 48 -- 4186, photograph 4186. That was already used in the examination-in-chief. I can't carry all these things with me. It's heavy anyway. Under the 65 ter, please, 4186.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think the document already has an exhibit number so it will be simpler to find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, a number has already been given to this document. May I just make a comment before the witness answers. This photograph, as we see it on the screen, is cut off because there's someone else to the left on this photograph whom we don't see on this photograph. There's somebody to the left. We come across this photograph all over the place.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know who the person to the left is and why the Prosecutor is providing such reduced photographs. I can't use exhibit numbers because I still haven't received a list of exhibits, and when documents are admitted into evidence, I should be given such a list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, when the Prosecutor asked for this photograph to be admitted into evidence, the Registrar gave it a number. Maybe it escaped you but a number was given. But that is not so very important. Yes, Mr. Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the reduced picture, it is a still taken from a video clip and so necessarily it is only a part of the video. There was no intention of cutting off parts of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, would you proceed with your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, Mr. President, the Prosecutor should have given us the video and then we could talk about the video rather than a photograph which the Prosecutor made on the -- from the video, and I think that is not appropriate. But I now wish to ask the witness something else so can I have the photograph on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You can see here four soldiers and one civilian; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: One soldier is quite far in the background so you can't see him very well and possibly there's another soldier behind this soldier on the left because we can see some boots.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't see anything on my screen yet so I can't answer that. Yes, I have it now. I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief, when looking at these two soldiers - one on the left and one behind - you said that they were JNA soldiers, and you said that the right -- the soldier on the right was a Chetnik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say anything about the one behind. I can't see him. I spoke about the one on the left and the one on the right. And the one on the right, I said that because of the cap he was wearing I would rank him in that category. That's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mm, I see. Now, do you see that these two soldiers do not have a five-pointed star on their helmets. Did you notice that?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And can you see that instead of that wiped-out five-pointed star, the cockade has been stuck on their helmets. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we have to be quite honest and can't say what it is that's being attached. Maybe it's a flag, a Serbian flag. Maybe it's a white star.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, it can't be a white star. The communist pointed star was red.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I made a slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, red, blue and white would have been the Serbian flag. It's in colour, so quite obvious if there is no colour in itself the Serbian flag, and it's a double-headed white eagle. That's the Serb emblem?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's possible, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, since these two soldiers have the Serbian coat of arms instead of the red five-pointed star, then they could be called Chetniks, too, couldn't they?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could, but I have distinguished them in the way I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you see that the soldier on the right has some strange insignia on his cap? I've never seen one like that. Do you know what it is, perhaps? Because it's not a Serbian coat of arms.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combined with the cap, as far as I'm concerned - and I say it's a Chetnik cap - so once again I'm giving you my opinion. I can't do more than that, nor did I claim when I was questioned earlier on that that was it 100 per cent. But as far as I was concerned that's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, you don't have to have this defensive mechanism. I do accept your testimony basically, and I think that 90 per cent of what you said was the truth, and I can tell you that straight away. So there's no reason for you to put up this defensive barrier. Let's clarify this together because I find it strange, too, and I feel the need to clarify this by talking to you. So as to relativise this division that you make between the JNA soldiers, the territorials, and the Chetniks, because I don't think that you have provided sufficient grounds to separate these three groups. But I accept your testimony as being 90 per cent correct and everything that you say happened to you personally, I consider that you weren't lying. So I hope I can settle your mind with respect to that and perhaps these things don't seem to be too serious as far as you're concerned, but they're very serious for me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So let's have that photograph back again, please. May we have the photograph back on our screens?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see it on two screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Oh, well, you're privileged with respect to me because I have it only on one screen. Anyway, the soldier on the right, can you see that he has the complete uniform of the JNA except the helmet or soldier's cap?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, correct. If you listened to what I was saying, I said it was because of the cap that I would place him in the category I placed him in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you very short questions and they require short answers. You don't have to go into any explanations, but we'll take it step by step, in detail. I have two and a half hours at my disposal so I want to deal with all the details. We quite obviously see a JNA uniform and it's an old olive-green uniform, the old SMB, olive-green uniforms.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Over that we have a flak jacket, do we not?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that is of a newer date because it's a camouflage bullet-proof vest.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, these two soldiers have the classical olive-green JNA uniform.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, you ought to know that until 1991 the JNA exclusively wore this type of uniform, the SMB or olive-green uniform.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that in the second half of 1991 the JNA started producing camouflage uniforms on a large scale.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you also know that for instance in one JNA unit some of the soldiers would be wearing the old SMB olive-green uniforms and the other soldiers would be wearing these new camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. So you're clear on that and you're not challenging that.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So do you agree that on the basis of this photograph we cannot say with any certainty whether these are, in fact, JNA soldiers - I'm referring to these two - doing their regular military service --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object, Mr. President. The witness has already answered the question as to which group the soldiers belonged to. He was asked this on a number of occasions. He said that was his feeling; he said why. And I object to having this question put yet again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Seselj, the accused, said that in his opinion they were members of the JNA, so don't ask him the same question 10 times. I'll put a question to you because it's important. We have a photograph here and we can see four individuals, plus an elderly person with a walking stick who was a prisoner accompanying them. We don't really know. But these four soldiers, one of which isn't wearing a helmet, in your opinion are they members of the JNA or the Territorial Defence or are they volunteers? What would you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my opinion, let me repeat, he belongs to a Chetnik formation. That's my opinion and I repeat that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in your opinion, even though they're wearing olive-drab uniforms and have helmets, they're Chetniks. Very well. All four of them or the one with the sort of cap on his head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, just the one with the cap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The one with the cap, he belongs to a Chetnik unit, to the Chetnik units, and the others are JNA members is what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I'm concerned, when I see this cap I would think that it was somebody belonging to a Chetnik formation. That's how I see things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the soldier with the cap. But what about the four others that we can see wearing drab-olive clothing? Are they Chetniks or JNA members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, those others would not, as far as I'm concerned, be members of the Chetnik formations. Either the JNA or reservists, but I think they're a bit too old. But it's difficult to say whether they're regular soldiers or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're making my cross-examination impossible. When the Prosecution asked even the most ludicrous questions you did not intervene, whereas, as far as I'm concerned, all these questions are very important because I want to make the witness' assertions more relative and how he distinguishes between JNA soldiers, Chetniks, and territorials. I'm going to stay with this photograph for a long time so, Judge, sir, don't call this person a prisoner. He's quite obviously an elderly man who is a civilian whom the soldiers probably found in some cellar, as the line -- front line moved, and they took him out. They're not cocking a weapon at him, he's not tied, and there's nothing to show that he's a prisoner of any kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I didn't say he was a prisoner. I said that there were two possible situations. He could be a prisoner, because you can see that he is surrounded in the photograph, but there's another possibility: He could be accompanied by these men. That's what I said. So we don't know what situation this person is in exactly. But that's not the problem. The problem is whether the soldiers we can see are members of the JNA, of the Territorial Defence, or of a Chetnik unit, which is what the witness seems to be saying, at least for one of them, the one with the cap on his head. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you exclude the possibility that these soldiers with the helmets are Chetniks, too?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot exclude that possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. Now, since you were at an officer's post, you weren't an officer officially in Vukovar but you were the commander of a squad which is an officer position?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It was a junior officer, non-commissioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, have you heard that there was a Chetnik unit with the official title "Chetnik unit" in Vukovar on the other side?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I hadn't heard about that. Not with this official title.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you couldn't have heard about that because you will probably agree with me if I tell you that that kind of unit never existed. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all right. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There was the 1st Guards Brigade opposite you with units of the Territorial Defence and volunteers attached; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who was against us and opposite us in those terms.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at a 65 ter photograph number 4245 now, please. Now, since you need quite a lot of time for that, may we have 6033 which is a video clip. I'm going to ask that that be shown after the photograph. So 6033 after the photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, on this photograph we can see that civilian, and obviously it's an elderly man, right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And quite obviously he is an invalid because he's carrying a stick.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one can assume that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he was probably sick, because if you look at his face he was probably sheltering in cellar for a long time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, next to him you see two soldiers and one is wearing a camouflage uniform without a cap or helmet on his head; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the other is a soldier wearing an SMB, olive-green uniform, with a helmet. Now, can you see that where you would expect to see a five-pointed star there is none?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, can you see part of this emblem, the double-headed eagle, white eagle on the helmet, up at the top?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we have -- see the top of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But the videotape would be better, but for some reason the Prosecution doesn't want to show you that.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can just see half a helmet, to be quite frank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You have the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we chose a still image to save time, but we can show the video if you so desire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Seselj, we do have the video. If you like we can see the video, we can look at it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let's have the video played.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You saw this clip and it's taken somewhere up at the front line or near the front line. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So the soldiers are taking away a civilian from the front line and are passing towards an area that is safer, so there's no snipers or anything else.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite possible. It can be a number of situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, do you exclude the possibility that these other soldiers are Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they were similarly dressed and they look like the one I said that, as far as I'm concerned, they don't look like a Chetnik. But if I'm quite frank, I can just see a white blodge on the helmet, so I don't know what insignia there is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that on the opposite side, on the enemy side, very rarely did anybody wear a cap or sajkaca, that most of them wore a helmet?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want to interrupt Mr. Seselj, but he's putting a question of a very general nature, which group did the other soldiers belong to that -- we watched a video. There are a lot of soldiers who we can see and we don't really know who is concerned. Perhaps Mr. Seselj could state which soldier he has in mind when we watch the video, because I'm not quite sure which soldier we are discussing exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Karlovic, that very rarely did any soldier, whether we're talking about JNA soldiers or territorials or volunteers, that very few soldiers had the fur cap, or sajkaca; that you would see that now and again but infrequently? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the fighting itself that is correct. That was rare to see. But when the town fell, then there were a lot of this type -- there was a lot of this type of insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, so somebody might have put a sajkaca, fur cap, on his head who had never worn it before.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can't expect me to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right, fine.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now let's have a look at the video clip 6033

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "REPORTER: Amongst the horror, there is a surreal incongruity of celebration. Extremist Serb militiamen and women posing triumphantly for an end-of-battle photograph before returning to a morning feast of music and laughter, fuelled by alcohol. The motto on their flag is 'Freedom or Death' and they vow they will fight on."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop it there, please. We'll go back to the beginning again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In your opinion, what unit is this? Is this a JNA unit or is it a Territorial Defence unit or a volunteer unit?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was thinking the same thing, what they were viewing this footage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, quite obviously it is a unit on the enemy side, right? Do you really consider these to be soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why wouldn't they be soldiers? Well, I don't know what answer to give you to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You don't know what they are?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I'll tell you what I think, and then I'm going to ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. You're going too fast. The court reporter is finding difficult to follow you in English. Mr. Seselj, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You saw that most of them had helmets, right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, somebody is wearing either a subara, a fur cap, or a sajkaca, a peasant cap?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, several of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And they have a Chetnik flag, right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And there are girls among them, too, right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it obvious that -- isn't it obvious, then, that these are volunteers?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Because there were no females in the JNA. Girls didn't do their regular military service?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And girls weren't reservists either, were they?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And they weren't in the Territorial Defence, were they?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that need not be a strict rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mean if someone reported as a volunteer, a girl. So quite obviously we're talking about volunteers and they're gathered together in one particular location; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And they're celebrating their victory; is that true?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, do they look inebriated to you? Are they drunk?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say. I can see that there's some alcohol.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, did you see that there was just one bottle of alcoholic beverage?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, from the clipping that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, is it possible that the foreign journalist who took this footage gave them a bottle of cognac?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm being asked to speculate. How do I know whether that was the case? How can you know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I'm just guessing you and asking your assistance.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say either. Everything is possible, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, obviously they had gathered together there and they had to go somewhere, right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, speculation. We're assuming something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, of course we're assuming something.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. You're going too fast. Our interpreters are very vigilant, very competent, but you are going too fast.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just saying yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but wait until Mr. Seselj has put his question and wait for a few seconds before you answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now an important question that concerns this footage. Compare -- well, this was probably taken on the 18th, 19th, or 20th of November. Compare these people here, what expressions they have on their faces, their excitement, and so on, and compare them to the soldiers at Ovcara, whether we're dealing with the JNA soldiers, territorials, Chetniks, or whatever you called them. Do they appear to you to be the same? Are they in the same mood? Do they have the same facial expressions? Do they seem to have the same intentions?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at this footage it's impossible to say. It's impossible to answer the question you've just asked me. I remember what it was like at Ovcara and how much desire there was for -- to have our blood, for our blood, and later on I saw some films with flags and they sang songs, such as "bring out the salad and we'll have meat because we're going to slaughter the Croats." But I can't say whether the expressions on their faces are the same, because people are singing here, whereas over there they went out to kill.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I agree. I just wanted to hear your answer. Now, you mentioned the song. How does it go? "Oh, Slobo, Croats we will slaughter and then eat, so send us some salad to go with the meat." Now, have you ever heard this song before the war sung at football stadiums, for example Mr. Karlovic?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You haven't heard it?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I never went to football matches.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But do you know a similar song sung by Croat football fans, where it says, Kill, kill Serbs?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we're talking about football stadiums here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But these are very similar songs and each side has their own song that they sing; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karlovic, at Ovcara you were afraid, you had to go through a very difficult situation, but what I'm interested in is this: Could you notice that the people who joined in the beating, that they knew many of the prisoners personally?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They knew them, didn't they? That means that they had some personal scores to settle; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That they were locals, inhabitants of the same town?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, some of them knew them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So they had -- there was this mood of revenge and retaliation, and that mood could have been based in something that had gone on in Vukovar previously; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really say. I wasn't in Vukovar before. I came from Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I see. According to your testimony, you saw officers there, too, JNA officers, did you not?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When the beatings stopped you said that the officers started making a list of the prisoners in Ovcara. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The fact that they made a list, started making a list, could that mean that a decision on execution had not yet been made, because would anybody compile a list before people were to be executed and shot?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The witness is being asked to speculate. I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's very speculative, a hypothetical question, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, speculation. Mr. Karlovic is an officer, has many years of war experience, and he can say on the basis of his own experience in Ovcara to draw conclusions. You've always allowed that so far when it comes to previous witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Put your question to the witness again, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, from the logical point of view, if the intention existed already that this group of prisoners should be executed, that you would have officers coming in -- them to be beaten first, then officers to come in, sit down to a table and draw up a list, isn't that a bit strange?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Maybe it is strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you find it strange as a soldier yourself?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't find it strange because I was never in that kind of situation, so I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And isn't it a little strange again that this group of soldiers - and you said they were JNA, territorials, Chetniks, and so on - that they brutally beat the prisoners and then that these prisoners were later executed? If they knew they were going to be executed and shot, why would they beat them first?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seselj, it was a vampire ball. It wasn't enough to just kill them but to belittle them and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I agree that this is quite wild and brutal behaviour and I'm not challenging the crime. I have never challenged it. A terrible crime did take place and there's no doubt about that. All I'm trying to do is to look at the circumstances, to investigate the circumstances of the event.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what other answer to give you other than the one I've given you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, that's an answer, too, yes. Now, Mr. Karlovic, you got married just before the war; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you wore your wedding ring. You took it to the battlefield with you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And it's on your left hand, left finger; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You're a Roman Catholic?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the Roman Catholics wear their wedding band on their left hand; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that we orthodox Serbs wear our wedding bands on our right hand?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite frankly, I have absolutely no idea about that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, the public does. That's enough. Now, let's continue with this clip, please. The videotape, let's see more of it

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And look at this man carefully. Can you see his left hand?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you see the wedding band on his left hand?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see a ring. Whether it's a wedding band, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you know what a wedding band looks like, don't you?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you call the wedding band a "burma" right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a wedding band and I know what "burma" means.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, it's a gold ring without any gemstones or --

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No adornments. It's just a gold band.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you see it on his left hand?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is he an orthodox -- of the orthodox faith?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say. It would be strange if I were to say anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But he has his wedding band on his left hand as the Roman Catholics do; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's on his left hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution can also look into how the orthodox Serbs wear rings. I'm not going to deal with this any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now I'll move on to some more specific questions with respect to what happened to you over there. In the course of examination-in-chief here you mentioned the Mitnik Battalion; is that right? The Mitnik Battalion surrendered entirely?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were a day or two at Ovcara before us. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And they all went to Sremska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: To the civilian prison that was taken over by the army for prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes. The others didn't want to surrender so they went to the Vukovar Hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the difference is that at the location I was in we weren't organised, whereas Mitnica was still organised. There was no command in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The Mitnica detachment surrendered, according to all the regulations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you mentioned Stuka, you described the manner in which he was dressed, and you said that he had combined various articles of clothing. He had some -- parts of a uniform on him and also civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I said he had a short jacket. It resembled a pilot's jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But that was not the uniform of someone from the air force.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite clear. The jacket was unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you know that Stuka was a JNA soldier.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was serving his regular military service; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if what he said is correct, then that's the case. But he introduced himself to me as Ilija, that he wasn't Ilija, and that can be understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: His name was Spasoje?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, his name was Spasoje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As a JNA soldier he wasn't dressed according to the JNA regulations, at least not completely; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it seems to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So in the wartime situation one didn't pay too much attention to the way one was dressed, to whether one was dressed correctly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And on your side you also had soldiers who were dressed in various manners; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my unit we were mostly all in uniform, but in other units they could be dressed differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There were some who fought in blue uniforms or blue overalls.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were from the regular police force. I don't know how many of them there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I saw some of them who had been killed in such clothes.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think they were members of the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And there were some HOS forces, Paraga's paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And they also had their own particular uniforms?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did they wear black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't, as far as I can remember. They were also wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So they went part of your regular unit. You were the ZNG, the home guards unit.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You had Borovo yellow boots on you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We took them in Vukovar subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They were very good boots?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They were newer?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all newer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you give them to Stuka?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did he give you his footwear?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't give me his footwear. He took some boots or shoes from a pile and gave them to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What sort of arms did Stuka carry?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, he had a large-calibre rifle, perhaps a Browning or an action shotgun.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that the JNA didn't have such rifles in their -- as part of their regular weapons, these pump-action rifles?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know -- well, these are details that I'm not familiar with. I didn't really know what sort of weapons the JNA had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. If I tell you that the JNA didn't have such weapons, would you believe me?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's no reason for me not to believe you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did the ZNG have a certain number of pump-action rifles?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, we didn't have such pump-action rifles. I'm talking about my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: About your unit. I understand. If I said I myself saw that our forces had captured a certain number of such pump-action shotguns, would you believe me?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So in that case, if Stuka really had a pump-action shotgun, would it be possible to say that this was a war booty?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible. I'm waiting a bit before I answer because I don't want to be too fast. But I must repeat that I still have this pump-action shotgun in my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These questions put to the witness call for speculation and I object to this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not asking for the witness to speculate. I'm putting questions to him and he answers these questions to the best of his ability and on the basis of his experience. I'm not asking the witness to do anything. If he doesn't want to answer a question, I can't force him to do so. I don't think this objection is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, do continue. I can't really see where you're trying to go in when asking these questions about pump-action shotguns, but you certainly have something in mind. But if you fail to make use of it, we will have wasted a lot of time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have already succeeded in doing much. I hope you will understand that. The witness is confirming my theory that it was not possible to distinguish regular JNA soldiers, members of the Territorial Defence, and volunteers, very clearly on the basis of their external appearance. I have managed to demonstrate this and I am now moving on. If that's all I have managed to demonstrate in the course of my cross-examination, I have good reason to be very satisfied. Mr. President, should I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We'll now skip a certain number of events and we'll deal with the carpentry workshop from which you were taken out by a group of Chetniks. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You concluded that they were Chetniks on the basis of their external appearance; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They told me they were Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did they tell you they were volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't tell me that, naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did any one of them ever mention the Serbian Radical Party while you were with them?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I didn't say that they had mentioned that party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm not accusing you of anything. I just want us to be clear about everything here. When they took you there to some house in Petrova Gora they subjected you to torture?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And while torturing you, Marko Ljuboja accidentally appeared and saw what they were doing to you. He appeared by chance.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He appeared -- he turned up a little later. First of all someone objected in the house and then left, and then Marko Ljuboja turned up and Predrag Milojevic, also known as Kinez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They arrived together?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they arrived together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So could one assume that the person who objected left the house, met them and told them what had happened?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I found out later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the two men, Marko Ljuboja, and Predrag Milojevic, Kinez, appeared and tried to save you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And they took certain risk?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You said there were about 20 people there who were Chetniks and who tortured you.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And they also said that they were Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes. And you want to confirm that. But there were only two men here on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Kinez had an automatic rifle and Marko Ljuboja only had a pistol; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And these 20 so-called Chetniks were all armed?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Predrag Milojevic, Kinez; and Marko Ljuboja, Mare, were on one side, and they had pointed their weapons at the others, and there were another 20 on the other side who were pointing their weapons at these two men; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I provide you with a more detailed answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they entered the room they didn't point their weapons at each other immediately. It didn't come to that immediately. When we left the house, when we went out of the house, things became more tense. That's when they pointed their weapons at each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: At one point in time you mentioned someone called Belgija. He was the one who tortured you most actively?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He took me out and he was the person who tortured me most actively.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And Kinez put a question to him and said "Belgija, did you capture him at the front line?" He was being cynical?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you understand this in the same way that I understood it?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believed that Kinez was mocking Belgija's military skill and his courage. Belgija fled from the front line, he couldn't have captured you from the front line? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: You're going too fast.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We're being warned again. We'll slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As far as I have understood this, Belgija never went to the front line, he fought somewhere in the rear, and if he got hold of a prisoner, that wasn't good for the prisoner. Would I be correct to say that this was frequently the situation in this war, on the Serbian end and on the Croatian side? Quite frequently the real soldiers didn't commit crimes, at least not generally speaking, whereas cowards, who weren't very efficient at the front line, committed crimes. Am I correct? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you what I know on the basis of my own experience, on the basis of what I saw on my side. In Vukovar as a prisoner I can draw the conclusion that that is the case, but naturally can't make such claims and say that it's a hundred per cent certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I just wanted you to comment on my opinion. Nothing else. In the course of that discussion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, Witness. The question that Mr. Seselj has put to you is an important one which could have subsequent consequences. The people who tortured you, who beat you, did you feel -- did you have the impression that these people had been on the front line? Because you were engaged in combat, so you could have noticed whether they had been in a situation in which they had to open fire, or were these people who were members of a reserve force, who had not fought and who maltreated prisoners? My question is very precise. The people who maltreated you, in your opinion, had they already fought at the front line? Had they already been at the front line previously?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. Seselj, I never asked myself whether they had fought, whether they were cowards. All I know is that they tortured me, and the last thing that I wanted to think about at the time was whether they were cowards or fighters.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, this firey discussion started between Kinez and Mare on the one side and the 20 so-called Chetniks on the other side. It became so tense that they pointed their weapons at each other; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If the soldiers who are the same -- were just as good, well, would two soldiers have been able to oppose 20?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I previously said that I thought that Kinez and Mare were people who exercised authority, Kinez in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But they weren't from the same unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's what was said on the occasion. Let me remind you of the trial in Belgrade. It was confirmed there. And you testified there on behalf of Kinez and Mare.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't think I said that because I thought they were from the same unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We'll consult the transcript.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. It's possible. I know they're not from the same unit. Later on this is what I found out. I learnt that they weren't from the same unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But they were two heroes, that's quite obvious, and they inspired fear and respect when they appeared; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, given what they did for me, I really believe that they're heroes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Would you also say they were ready to die in order to save you?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had that impression. I thought they were ready to die in order to save me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And although there were 20 men on the other side, they were afraid and no one opened fire in the end; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So they were cowards. They had commenced something. They outnumbered the others but they then gave way, so they were cowards. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could say that they were cowards. We could also say that reason prevailed. I know that Kinez said, Well, brothers, we're not going to start opening fire on each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Given the way that they tortured you, would you draw the conclusion that they were cowards and pathological men?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Because a normal person wouldn't do such a thing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When they were taking you away from Petrova Gora --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to clarify something. In the question that was put that concerns the fact that you were tortured, "given that you were tortured, would you say that they were cowards and psychopaths," there's a double question and when the witness replies we don't know what he's replying to exactly. Could we break the question up?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Seselj, there were two parts to your question. You can be a coward without being a psychopath and you can be a psychopath without being a coward and you can be both at the same time. So we have several variations, several possibilities. If you believe this is important, could you perhaps break your question up into two questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness understood me correctly. An ordinary coward would have fled, but a coward who is a psychopath flees from the front line, but he can hardly wait for the opportunity to torture a prisoner or someone who is helpless. The witness understood me correctly. There's no reason for me to repeat my question. I'll move on, with your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the people who tortured you, in your opinion, were they cowards? Were they psychopaths? Were they both at the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they are the worst kind of people for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: For me, too. So we agree. We can move on. They're the worst kind of people for me, too, whether you believe me or not. When they were taking you from Petrova Gora, Kinez and Mare said -- told you that these people were betraying the tradition of old Serbian soldiers. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They spoke about the heroic traditions behind them and these people were shaming those traditions; is that right.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember which unit Predrag Milojevic, Kinez, and Marko Ljuboja, Mare, belonged to?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know they were volunteers, but I don't know which unit they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Had you heard of the Leva Supoderica detachment?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And at the trial in Belgrade you heard that they belonged to this detachment?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know, Mr. Karlovic, that at the Vukovar theatre of war all volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party were exclusively members of the Leva Supoderica detachment?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite frankly I must admit that I didn't know that they belonged to the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm not saying that these two belonged to the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the detachment. I didn't know that the members of the detachment were members of the Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you don't have to know these things. Anyway, I will now read out a paragraph from the records of the trial in Belgrade. This was happening in your presence. You made your statement and then Marko Ljuboja and Predrag Milojevic, Kinez, asked you certain questions; is that right? This happened in Belgrade. You greeted them warmly there.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, I did.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have this document, provided to me by the Prosecution, but I don't have the ERN number. It is the audio-recording from the 13th of September, 2005, the chamber for war crimes of the district court in Belgrade. You can find it. It is page 32-45, so could you place it on the ELMO. But I don't have the ERN number. Is that a problem for the Registry? It may be of interest to place this document on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it would be better to show the document on the ELMO because the registrar tells me that they cannot trace it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't put my document under the ELMO. What am I going to read, then? I have several pages marked here from which I wish to quote. Perhaps the Prosecutor has a copy of this document, because I received it from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please put your question on the basis of your document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You heard there that Marko Ljuboja presented his version of events in the house of Petrova Gora, and then the presiding judge asked you to express your views about it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then Marko Ljuboja said --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you found it? It is page 32/45. Yes, that's it. 32/45. The paragraph is 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Never mind, you've already confirmed that -- all that contained in this paragraph. Marko Ljuboja describes the situation. You were sitting, stripped to the waste, et cetera. But the last paragraph on that page, Marko Ljuboja describes his motives for saving you. Would you like to read out what he said? Do you know the Cyrillic script? If it's a problem I'll do it?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At that moment he was a Croatian prisoner of war and nothing more than that for me. For me, therefore, he was a Croatian, enemy soldier, who was captured and I would not allow him to be killed in that way. Nothing more than that. Therefore, there was no other reason for us to save him. At that moment when we drew our weapons, if Villem remembers, I had my pistol cocked and they held their rifles pointed at us and we walked along the whole corridor in that way, pointing our weapons at each other." Is that the truth?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then you go on to say -- now, would you read out the first paragraph from the next page, what you said.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "And in that way we reached the yard and you pushed me -- you put me on your back" --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, this must be an error. It says here "on your back." But "behind your back they had their weapons -- they had their weapons pointed at each other." And then there was an exchange of swear-words, is that right, between those who were saving you and those who were torturing you?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then Marko Ljuboja mentions the swear-words used, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mothers were sworn at and then they could kill me, across their dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's what Kinez said, you can kill them over our dead bodies. You can see it later that Marko Ljuboja says that that is what Kinez said. Have you found that place?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have. Mare asks me: "Did Kinez say you can kill him over our dead bodies?" And I say yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you went through the door, some jumped through the window to be quicker.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that, but that is what Marko Ljuboja says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you remember? Can you see that on this page?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It says here, but it's not very important if you haven't found it. Let's go back to what you said. Marko Ljuboja asks you: "Did he apologise to you, and why?" And your answer is the sixth brief paragraph from the top. The witness answers -- could you read that out, please. It's what you said.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment for me to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: "Are you apologising to me?"

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I read it out?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "If you apologise, because if you were a Serb that believes in God, because everything that was happening and did happen was not being done by all Serbs, and then you apologised to me on behalf of the entire Serbian nation."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then Marko Ljuboja goes on. Would you read it?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then Marko Ljuboja asks me: "Did I say that I apologised on behalf of Serbia in the First World War? Because the Serbian army never did any such things." And my answer is: "Quite so. I now remember."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then he talks about the traditions of the Serbian army. We won't go into that. Move on to the next page, please. Yes, the next page. Now, the third paragraph from the bottom, the presiding judge asks Marko Ljuboja: "Who are those men, if you know?" And then will you read what Marko Ljuboja says?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I don't know who those men are. I came there because my soldier, Plave, told me that they are having fun and throwing grenades and that people couldn't sleep, and I thought it was my unit doing this. When I entered I found these men and that is why they reacted in that way and said, 'This is not your unit. This is not your prisoner.'"

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, please move on two pages forward. It's page 36/45. Here, Predrag Milojevic, Kinez, he tries to explain which unit it was. Could you read that out too, please? If you're tired, I can do it. But as these are your friends and saviours --

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, please be kind enough to read it. Page 36/45. At the top of the page, please, the first line. Predrag Milojevic, Kinez, is speaking.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "As far as the composition of those men is concerned, I'd like to make an explanation, I'd like an explanation." And the president asks: "Who were those men?" Milojevic answers: "I know their nicknames, Belgija, Spasoje."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You probably heard those names and you confirm that.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said I heard of Belgija. "Spasoje, Belgija, Ciga," says Milojevic. "There was a woman in that room." This is what I said. Milojevic says, "I don't remember the woman. There was an elderly man from Vinkovci, known as Cica."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mentioned Cica?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Miljan or Miljan, but I did say that he was an elderly man.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then what do you go on to say?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a minute, please, you're going too quickly. Start up again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You say that Cica tied you.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't tied for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you sure that you said that?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I'm just showing you the transcript. Where does it say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: After Predrag Milojevic, who mentions Cica, and then you say, "that one tied me up."

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I said that one cut me up. That must be a mistake in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I believe you, sir. I'm just pausing. Can we move on?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So there's an error in the notes here. You said this one cut me up, not tied me up. And what does Predrag Milojevic say after that?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
