utterances.text: "The older man from Vinkovci, Cica, who also argued fiercely with me and who held his pistol, not the rifle," because when I said they couldn't do this, they picked up their weapons. However, I said: "Don't touch your weapons. At that moment Mare held his pistol like this, if you recall," and my answer is, "yes, I do." Then Milojevic says I said that I caught him and pushed him behind me because I didn't dare put him next to Karlovic so that someone who may be drunk wouldn't open fire arbitrarily. I don't quite understand this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then the presiding judge asks: "Yes, but who were those men, Mr. Milojevic? And then Milojevic answers. Will you read that?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milojevic says: "I tell you, they were men from Vinkovci. This Cica himself was from Vinkovci. Then there was a Zolja, if you remember." And then I answer: "I don't remember that one." Shall I go on?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "There were some five or six young men. I referred to them when I said, Aren't you ashamed to torture such a man in the presence of these children who were so young, and they were standing in the left corner, if you remember." And I say "Yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then Milojevic says: "Ceda answered, I will use some bad language now and he says, Who fucks their mother? Let them get stronger. Is that right?" And then you answer "yes?" You said that Ceda and Belgija were the most aggressive. And then what Pedrag Milojevic says. Ceda and Belgija, and then there was someone with a nickname. Remember, this is a unit from Vinkovci. And then Predrag Milojevic, Kinez, says that it was a unit from Vinkovci"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what could that unit be, a unit from Vinkovci, which was never under Serb control during the war?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not under Serbian control because as far as I know more than 90 per cent of the population were Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, but there was a group of Serbs who fled from Vinkovci and who formed a unit. We can conclude that from this. Vinkovci is west of Vukovar, right, so they're not in Serbia, they're not volunteers from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fortunately they were not. Fortunately that Vinkovci is not part of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No, what I mean is fortunately that they were not volunteers from Serbia, so here we are on different sides.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What's the problem now? We are too quick?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT REPORTER
utterances.text: I'm having difficulty figuring out who's speaking and what is being quoted. Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please, as this is an important point. It should be included in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Please follow me closely. I will repeat slowly. So Vinkovci is a town in Slavonia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Throughout the war Vinkovci were under Croatian control. They were never under Serb control; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: A certain percentage of Serbs did live in Vinkovci. I don't know the exact percentage. Not many anyway. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know a very small percentage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But a certain number of Serbs had fled Vinkovci.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And Predrag Milojevic, Kinez, says here that those Serbs had formed a unit; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So the men who tortured you, according to Predrag Milojevic, Kinez, were people from Vinkovci.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Belgija introduced himself and said he was from Belgrade and that he was a leader of the Fans of Partizan, a football club.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You know he could have said anything to you, but we're discussing here what happened at the proceedings in Belgrade. He could have used my name in introducing himself; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but you're asking me to confirm that they were from Vinkovci. Some may have been, some not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to confirm this. We're just going through the transcript of the proceedings in Belgrade. You don't know those men.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So we are going through the transcript of your testimony in Belgrade. That is what is important for me. Because I was not familiar with any of those events until I saw your statement. Do you believe me?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why wouldn't you believe me?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: For me the people who are familiar with the facts are important for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a minute. Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness didn't know those men, but I think if we wish to put this evidence before the Chamber, it would be appropriate for the accused to call these witnesses who testified in those proceedings and who describe the origin of the unit. Otherwise questions being -- that would be the best way to put questions and cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there is no point in this objection. I'm using a document here that was given to me by the Prosecution to use, and the Prosecution is not going to tell me who I will call as defence witnesses. I will call those I wish. I am now cross-examining a Prosecution witness and using documents given to me by the Prosecution, so I am acting quite appropriately. This witness is an eye-witness of the events in the courtroom in Belgrade, and he's telling us what happened in that courtroom. Is it time for the break, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Before the break I have a question for you, Mr. Witness. Before the judges of the court in Belgrade, according to the document we have in front of us, that the unit that tortured you in this carpentry shop were men from Vinkovci, a town which was not in Serbia and is in Croatia, and a reasonable judge could make the conclusion that those who tortured you were members of this unit. Nevertheless, it would appear that a certain point, this Belgija, the Belgian, told you that he was the leader of the Fans of the Partizan Football Club from Belgrade, and again a reasonable judge could draw the conclusion from this that this Belgija was not in fact a person from Vinkovci but that he originated from Belgrade. What is your feeling, if you have any? You may not, which we can fully understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't give thought to this matter of where they came from. I just know what Belgija told me. I didn't make any conclusions about Vinkovci. I heard about Vinkovci for the first time in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, did you ever in a statement mention that Belgija introduced himself as being from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I mentioned this, maybe not here, but I did mention it when I made my statement in Croatia. I don't know whether I mentioned it anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask you, Mr. President, to ask the Prosecutor to find in his documents during the break whether Mr. Karlovic ever said about Belgija that he came from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I help you? I think I didn't make such a statement here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Never?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case I don't need to ask the Prosecutor to do this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It is time for the break. We will have a 20-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. The first thing I wish to say, I wish the registrar to give us the time, that is, how much is left for Mr. Seselj. Secondly, I address Mr. Seselj and the witness. Please slow down the pace because, as you saw a moment ago, the interpreters and the court reporter had a great deal of difficulty. And before answering the question, Witness, please wait a few seconds. Count up to five before answering and that will give us a chance to record everything, because if it goes too quickly something very important, a word or a phrase, may not be recorded even though it may be of the greatest importance. That is what I wish to draw your attention to. Mr. Seselj has used one hour and 15 minutes and he has another one hour and 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, the last thing you said before the break was this: It was your confirmation that you'd never before stated that this man Belgija introduced himself as the leader of the Partizan football fans from Belgrade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I did say that in this trial. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you say it at some other trial, then?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I said it at any trial. I don't think I mentioned that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, perhaps it is true and correct because you happened to remember this at the time, but are you quite sure about that? Because I have a dilemma as soon as I decide to believe you. Mr. Karlovic, you know that quite a lot of Serbs from the territory of Croatia were fans of the Belgrade football clubs Partizan and Red Star, or Crvena Zvezda. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, I'm facing a dilemma. If I believe you, that Belgija actually said that to you, did he say that he was from Belgrade and that he was the leader of the Partizan football fans there, or was he the leader of the Partizan football fans from Vinkovci? What would you say?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I said was what he told me and the way in which he introduced himself to me. So let me repeat: He said to me that his name was Belgija, that he was from Belgrade, and that he was the leader of the Partizan football fans.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, during the break I contacted my associates and there are people there who are Partizan fans, and they said that there was never a Partizan supporter fan from Belgrade nicknamed Belgija. There was a man called Celzi and Combe and some other characteristic nicknames, but never a Belgija, or Belgian.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not claiming that either, nor is it important for me. All I'm doing is repeating what the man told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Seselj. Witness, judging by the accent of a person speaking Serbo-Croatian, can one tell whether he is from Belgrade or from a part of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, you can distinguish a Belgrade accent, or rather, a Serbian accent or a Croatian accent. Of course you can distinguish between the two accents, if I've understood your question correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you have. And in this particular case do you remember being able to make this distinction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wouldn't be proper of me if I said that I did recall whether the Ikavian or Ekavian accent was used, that would be out of place. I can't remember but I do know what the man said to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you exclude all possibility of him introducing himself as the leader of the Partizan fans, the Partizan from Belgrade, without saying that he was from Belgrade, too?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said from Belgrade, the Partizan football fans leader, and I repeat what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Fine, Mr. Karlovic. If you had already said that somewhere else I could examine you on that point, but I haven't found it anywhere in the documents or anywhere else. But it's not an essential point. Let's move on to page 37/45. Have you found the page? You see here the presiding judge, in the first paragraph, referring to Predrag Milojevic, a.k.a. Kinez, says that he went to see Lancuzanin and some others were with Bojkovski and Radic, and so on. And now in the fourth paragraph Predrag Milojevic is giving a more precise explanation as to which units these people were from, the people that tortured you, captured you with the intention of killing you. So would you look at that paragraph 4 and tell us what Predrag Milojevic says?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "A lot was talked about here about formations. A real conclusion was never reached as to what formations were active over there. You had over there units at Velepromet and certainly some 50 men who joined or did not join the units."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Pause there, please. How do you explain this?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I must say I didn't understand what this means, "joined or didn't join." I'm not clear on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I'm trying to understand this. There were 50 men who at one time were in certain units and sometimes they acted on their own.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the conclusion that could be drawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They were armed people, armed men, that were not included in any JNA units and forces under JNA control; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what Predrag says.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So these were some sort of outlaws, irregular fighters? Can you draw that conclusion as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Continue reading to the end of the paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "I said that they -- I said that I thought they joined the 2nd Company, that unit, that is to say, they were from within the composition of the other company. They were Negoslavcani and they belonged to the Negoslavacki Battalion. Because that man from Vinkovci, Cica, who was there, he belonged to the Negoslavci Battalion, because when we worked the settlement, the right side, I had a connection with him and he belonged to the Negoslavci Battalion."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you clear on the fact that when Predrag -- that Kinez said, "When we did the settlement," it meant they took control of the settlement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So when he took control of the settlement he came into contact with a Negoslavci Battalion; is that how you interpret that?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And in that Negoslavci battalion there was this man called Cica. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of the Territorial Battalion from Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it later on but not at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you agree that Predrag Milojevic identifies these people as members of the 2nd Company of the Battalion of the TO for armed Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is what Predrag said. That's all I have to go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you believe him?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is that what he said?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karlovic. Now, do you know where Negoslavci are located?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It's a village near Vukovar, right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down once again, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now let's take a look at something else. I have a question concerning the transcript, or rather the stenographic notes. Maybe we have finished with that area. It's not essential. Mr. Karlovic, you know that Marko Ljuboja, Mare, and Predrag Milojevic, Kinez, were tried in Belgrade for war crimes.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you also know that Predrag Milojevic, Kinez, as one of the commanders - I think he was come in as deputy - was given a prison sentence of 20 years?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that the only proof and evidence against him that they had was that on that day, prior to the crime, he was seen at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what proof they had and on what grounds he was found guilty. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, Predrag Milojevic, a.k.a. Kinez, and Marko Ljuboja, a.k.a. Mare, when they saved you, did they look to you like people who had just come back from Ovcara where they had spent the whole night executing people, and then they took it into their heads to save you? Is that the impression you gained?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already answered that question in Belgrade in a similar fashion. I simply don't believe that those people, after what they did for me, that they could be killers. I've already stated that. That is my opinion. That is what I think about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know the names of the other accused in the Belgrade trials? Are you familiar with their names?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite frank I don't know, except for one man who was a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right, then, we won't mention him. Now, is it clear to you that Predrag Milojevic, Kinez; and Marko Ljuboja, Mare; Milan Lancuzanin Kameni, their commander; and Slobodan Katic, as members of the Leva Supoderica detachment, were tried in Belgrade exclusively in order to create an artificial link between me and the crime in Ovcara. Is that quite clear to you?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just answer and say that I have heard about Kameni because a moment ago I said I didn't know of him. I know about Lancuzanin . As to what you're asking me now, I really don't know. I can't say whether those legal proceedings were undertaken to implicate you. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, in the theory of speech and rhetorics, there's a rhetorical question. You put the question but don't really expect an answer?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that you make ample use of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Karlovic. Now, let's look into something else, something that you introduced --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A small question, Witness. When you attended the proceedings in Belgrade, were you a witness of the prosecution or of the defence?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to object. It was the continental system and all witnesses are witnesses of the court. It is the court who decides who it's going to call as a witness, not the prosecution and not the defence. They cannot call witnesses independently. They make their proposals but it is the court that decides who's going to be on the list of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you received an order to appear before the tribunal, as Mr. Seselj says, was it indicated that the court is asking you to appear and not the prosecutor or the defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's like this. Let me try and explain in my own words, as I understood it. I was the first to say at the trial that I wasn't a witness either of the defence or of the prosecution but a witness of the truth, and the presiding judge, the president of the trial chamber, the judge, confirmed that, that I was there only to tell the truth, that I was neither a prosecution witness nor a defence witness. I hope that makes things clearer now, the way in which I have just answered your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, your answer is quite correct. Here, too, you're a witness of the truth, even though you have been called by the Prosecution. But my question was of a technical nature and that is, was it -- it was the tribunal who called you to appear and not the prosecutor or the defence. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was called by the court to appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, you described and commented on the Chetnik flag that was shown on the video clip, and you explained that you'd never seen a flag like that in Vukovar but that you had seen it on Croatian television. Now, have you ever seen or did you ever see the same flag twice, if we're not talking about the same footage? The same flag, the same insignia and everything else the same, were all those flags unique, devised according to somebody's image?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember. I just remember that black flag with the skull and bone emblem. But maybe I haven't understood your question properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If I tell you that from the 1990s onwards there was never a factory production of Chetnik flags, uniform factory manufacture, but that the flags were designed by individuals on a need-to-use basis, when they felt a need for a flag, would you believe me when I tell you that?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're putting me in a very difficult situation. Possible, not possible. Believe you, not believe you. Everything is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I won't belabour the point, then, and tire you with that. Let's move on to another question, another area, that you haven't mentioned yet, that you never mentioned before, and then suddenly it appeared in your consolidated statement. You know what question I'm relating to.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the loudspeaker.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes. We ought to clarify that now. You said that between the 10th and 15th of November --

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly, roughly around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said. Roughly between the 10th and 15th of November - we don't know exactly when - you said that on several occasions you heard my voice over the loudspeaker calling for a surrender.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard a voice similar to yours. Similar to yours, that sounded like your voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you're not certain that it was my voice?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not I'm certain, but it sounded like you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that that person said, "Ustashas surrender. There's no need for you to continue dying. Everything's over with the town so surrender so you shouldn't be killed for no reason."

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You know that when the war began in Vukovar there was no electricity, no electric power.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So how did this loudspeaker work? Was there a generator, separate generator of some kind?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it wasn't recorded, but I said that it appeared to me as if it was a loudspeaker attached to a vehicle, and you know yourself that for military purposes you can produce electric power whether there's any electricity or not in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karlovic, I know that, but I never heard of any loudspeaker system being used in Vukovar and that's not contained in any Prosecution witness' statement, whether they are crime-base witnesses or witnesses on the Serb side. So that seems a little strange, that suddenly you happen to remember that voice over this loudspeaker and the message, because I've never heard of this loudspeaker before.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to answer that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you could comment, give us your opinion, your impression.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can do is to repeat what I heard and how I heard it, and that's 100 per cent how it was. I just said that the voice was similar to your voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And how come you never remembered that in the many statements and testimonies you gave?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you one thing. There's always something that comes to mind and other things that you tend to forget, so that's it. Everything is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Perhaps you heard an interview of mine on the -- over the radio and then I might have said something similar that you should surrender, not to lay down your lives in vain, and so on.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I haven't had hallucinations like that yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right, fine, but I can't understand where you got this loudspeaker from?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, ask around. There were loud speakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You want me to ask around whether I spoke over the loud speaker?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. You said that you never heard of any loud speakers, and I said that you should ask around and you'll be given the information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, when I was walking around Vukovar I saw Major Sljivancanin using his Motorola radio station, for instance, and he talked to Jastreb, your commander, Dedakovic, right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, once again you are going too quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And once again you're testifying.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I want to ask the witness a question, whereas you're intervening straight away. I have the right to pose leading questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have the right, but put the question directly, not a monologue first and then a question. Go directly to the question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, since the witness isn't quite certain that he actually heard my voice, then there's no reason for me to waste time on that and belabour the point, so I'm moving on to another area, another question. I have received some more documents here from the Prosecution, so I'd like to have the following document, ERN number 0207-7562 placed on the overhead projector, please, and it is quite obviously a set of documents from the Croatian government. I don't know what ministry, whether the police or the defence ministry, but I was disclosed as part of that document. And I'm going to put the -- present the document to you here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the registrar can't find the document by using the ERN number, so it would be best to put the document on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all I have here is one example. I didn't make a photocopy because I thought that you had this. But then the registrar should supply me with it. Anyway, put this on the overhead projector. I have two questions I want to deal with it. First put this page on the overhead projector and then the next one and then I'll show you something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So this is an official document of the Croatian government that conducted an investigation into the events in Vukovar, and they presented their own version, of course. But what I'm interested in in this one sentence which they take note of on the basis of this investigation, that under the command of the 1st Guards Brigade -- now, let's see what's underlined here. That there were various volunteer Chetnik detachments, detachments of the Territorial Defence from the village of Negoslavci and from the Vukovar local community of Petrova Gora; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I just say what the point of this is so that you can give us your judgement. The Croatian government says that we're dealing with different volunteer Chetnik detachments, different ones, various ones. The accent is on the word "razni," different. Now, do you agree that that corresponds to what the situation was like in the field?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question. I do know there were Chetnik detachments. Whether there were different ones, I don't know. Probably volunteer ones. I don't know how to answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you consider all volunteer units to be Chetnik units?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, do you know that the Croatian politicians and Croatian propaganda in general called the JNA, for example, the Serbo-Chetnik or Yugo-Chetnik armada?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember that. Quite possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that on the Croatian side they called all Serb fighters Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't quite like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It wasn't, you say. Right. Now, do you know that the vast majority of the Serb fighters in this war was proud of being called Chetniks? They referred to themselves as Chetniks, regardless of which formations and units they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know who was proud and whether they were proud. I can't answer that and you have to respect that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you put yourself right during the testimony in Belgrade when you said Chetniks and then you said, I don't want to offend anybody.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends how people see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Would you turn to the next page, please, because I have underlined another sentence there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't got it up on my screen yet. It hasn't appeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Would you read out that sentence, please?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Many Chetniks at the beginning, in order to aggrandise their contribution to the liberation of Vukovar, introduced themselves falsely as executors and participants in a slaughter. In fact, in the slaughter numerous members of the 1st Guards Brigade of the JNA took part and the Territorial Defence who were subordinated to it."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Stop there. We're not interested in the rest. It deals with something else and not essential here. Is it clear to you in what way the Croatian authorities were -- identified the perpetrators of crimes?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All that's super, but I don't -- I know what saw in -- at Ovcara and I don't know what this has to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking your opinion of this?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can read it out and that's it. That's what it says. But I really don't know how I can answer that. What opinion do you think I ought to have concerning this?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Give me the document, please, and I'll tell you why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, read through the paragraph slowly again, because it went so fast that there is something that I missed. Could you read out everything that has been underlined, or even the paragraph from the very beginning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "After this event the Chetniks celebrated in the town of Vukovar, and the truth about this terrible crime rapidly spread throughout the Republic of Croatia. At the beginning many Chetniks, in order to aggrandise. Their contribution to the liberation of Vukovar, falsely presented themselves as the executors and participants of the slaughter. In fact numerous members of the 1st JNA Guards Brigade and TO units that were subordinated to it participated in the slaughter."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's all we wanted. We won't speculate about who is guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Witness, this report, which seems to be a Croatian government report -- well, it's an investigation that must have been carried out following the events in Vukovar, so we're talking about the Croatian side that compiled this report. It's not a Serbian report. And this report concludes that the crimes allegedly committed can be attributed to the JNA and to the Territorial Defence, and the report adds that Chetniks celebrated the victory - and this is what we saw in the video - but that in fact they pretended to be those involved in the event, but in fact it was the JNA and the Territorial Defence who were involved in the event. Would you agree with this conclusion or not? Do you contest this conclusion or is there nothing you can say about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't carry out this investigation myself, and secondly I was at the site in question and I do know that they all participated in crimes there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You say all of them participated, and that includes the Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those who tortured me claimed to be Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do not contest this, but the term Chetnik is far too wide, far too broad, and it only represents the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party. That's my point. I hope you understand me. Could I have this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, in what follows in the document, one can see that the document was compiled on the basis of your testimony as well. Unfortunately I don't have that on me. But the Croatian government says the other witnesses and then your name is the first one that appears. Please have a look at it. Is what I have said correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you give me the document back, please, and we'll move on to the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, before you came to testify in this case against me in The Hague, did some Croatian military or police department speak to you?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the last 10 years no one from Croatia has spoken to me. Let's say that that concerns the last 10 years, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But in the Mrksic, Sljivancanin, and Radic case, you confirmed that someone spoke to you before your testimony.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, before the very first testimony. Perhaps the information was erroneously conveyed. But after that initial conversation no one spoke to me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please place 0261-2957 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The registrar tells me that he can't find the document in the system, so it would be best to place the document on the ELMO. Mr. Seselj, do you have this document on you or not?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, but I'm really surprised to see that your electronic system isn't functioning correctly. Please could you place the first page on the ELMO first and then the other page that I have marked. But could we first have the title page on the ELMO. We need to see the entire page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, you can see that this is an official document from the Croatian Ministry of Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It is the security and information service. Its acronym is SIS, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's the military intelligence department; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, security and intelligence service.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We Serbs would say the military intelligence service.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I didn't personally obtain this document. You know that I don't have any access to the Croatian archives. The Prosecution provided me with this document. This document shows that the SIS of the Croatian Ministry of Defence participated in preparing you for your testimony in the Mrksic, Sljivancanin, and Radic case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please turn the page, have a look at the marked page and show that page to Mr. Karlovic. I've turned the corner of the page down so that you can find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Please read through the fifth paragraph, the last paragraph at the end, but don't -- read through the last paragraph at the end, section number 5, but don't mention the name of the person who appears after your name because he is a protected witness here and there is no reason for me to mention his name.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Section 5 at the end?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "This service participated in preparing the witnesses to confirm the indictment against Mrksic, Radic, and Sljivancanin, and in the case against Dokmanovic." And then there are names, my name --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Don't read out the second name, the other names. There's no need. You can see that in a SIS official document they confirm that they participated in preparing you for your testimony in the case against the so-called Vukovar 3; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Perhaps they're lying. I'm not going to go into that now. But what can I do? I have to use the documents that the Prosecution provided me with.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we didn't find out anything new. These are things that I already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You are being falsely presented as someone in whose preparation they participated.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You didn't understand me. I said I never denied this. This is what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did they participate in preparing you for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what they call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What do you call it?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't -- it wasn't necessary to prepare me. I had to say what happened to me in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So they prepared you or proofed you and you didn't take this to be proofing.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another document. The number is 0261-2928.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object, Mr. President. I wouldn't interpret the document as proofing, as preparation. I object to the idea that this document demonstrates that it was a matter of proofing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Witness, I'm a little lost. I'll tell you why. Initially you were asked whether you had met with the Croatian security services before this case. You said yes, but at the very beginning. That's what I understood, at the very beginning. And then Mr. Seselj asked you again whether you had met with them and you said no, so I thought you met them at the very beginning but not subsequently. And then we have a document that seems to show that -- I'll repeat what I said. Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll repeat everything.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Initially -- I'll summarize this. Initially you said, "I spoke to the security services at the very beginning," and then Mr. Seselj put the question to you again and you said, "No, I haven't seen them since then." And now we have a document that appears, and I underline the fact "appears," appears that to show that you had an interview with them in order to prepare you for the indictment or for the Mrksic case - I don't know what exactly - and I saw the date, the year 1999, in the document. So you must have met these people before 1999. So to clarify everything, in which year did you meet with members of the security service of your country? In which year exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My first answer is something you're not clear about, why I first said yes and then no and then yes. May I first answer that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said no, perhaps I misunderstood Mr. Seselj, but when I said no, that no concerned the question as to whether before I came to testify against him, against Mr. Seselj, I had contact of any kind with them and I said no. But I had contact with them in 1996 or 1997. I'm not quite sure of the year. That was the only time I spoke to them and I never spoke to anyone after that date. Is that clear now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I understand you, if I understand you correctly, in the last 10 years you have had -- you haven't had contact of any kind with them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No contact at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is in fact what the witness said, and it's on page 66, line 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, what would you like to demonstrate?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Antonetti, I'll move on, and when I finish with this section, you will see what I want to demonstrate. I can't say that in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, when testifying in the case of the Vukovar 3, Mrksic, Sljivancanin, and Radic, on the 21st of March, 2006, transcript page 6449, in that case when that question was put to you -- well, the question was: "Who did you give statements to two days before you came to testify in The Hague? To whom specifically?" And your answer was: "To two individuals who worked for that service, and I think one of them was Stjepan Udiljak and I know the other person's name is Tomislav, but I can't remember his surname." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Karlovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now have a look at another document. Would the usher be so kind as to put it on the ELMO. It's also from the SIS of the Ministry of Defence. Let's have a look at the title page first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You can see that it's an official document from the Croatian Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is there any reason for you to doubt the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, since it's a copy there are always reasons to doubt, but I don't doubt it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Have a look at the number the Prosecution put on the document in the right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. I trust you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I received this document from the Prosecution. It's marked as a state secret. Please have a look at the other marked page and have a look at the paragraph that has been marked.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You don't have to put it on the ELMO. We don't want to see the name of the protected witness, the name that appears after Mr. Karlovic's name. Can we see it internally without broadcasting it to the outside? Yes. Just a minute. It's the wrong side. Show the side that I marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's possible.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the page, the part that I have marked with a pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Please read through the title and the text, and don't mention the two names that appear after yours.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "This service participated in proofing the witness to confirm the indictment against Mrksic, Radic, and Sljivancanin and also to prepare the witness for the case against Dokmanovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And your name appears as the first name?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you return the document to me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, I showed you this because I'm convinced that in the case of your testimony in the case against me I believe that you were proofed for your testimony in this case against me in Zagreb. Is that correct? You're denying that?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am under oath and I know what the consequences of lying would be. I have no reason to lie, whether you believe me or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Unfortunately I don't have any proof to show that what you're saying is not correct, but thank you, Mr. Karlovic. I have a few other brief questions. When did you arrive in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 1st of October, between 3 and 4 in the morning in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: "Listopad" is what we Serbs say or call October.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say the tenth month.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. As soon as your name was disclosed I started investigating everything I could in relation to you.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Until recently you were listed as a protected witness in my case. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you ask for protective measures, for a pseudonym and everything else?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. On the first occasion I did make such a request, but when I realised that the Defence always had to know who was testifying, then protective measures had no sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The first time was in the Dokmanovic case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And at no point in time in the case against me did you require protective measures. Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I never requested protective measures.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a serious problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is there any way in which I could threaten you if I wanted to, even if I wanted to?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is always a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But it's a case of science fiction in this case.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you personally can't threaten me or present a danger to me, but there's always a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Very well. But at any point in time did you fear testifying in the case against me?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why do you think some other Croats called by the Prosecution as witnesses in this case, why do you think these other witnesses testified with the benefit of protective measures?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object. The witness is being asked to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, without speculating, fear is perhaps something one can quantify, and the question put to you was whether you were afraid at any point in time and you said no, never.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you testified in Belgrade, in the Kameni et al case, there were no problems. You arrived in Belgrade, you went to the court, and then you left. Everything went smoothly, or were there any problems?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court offered me protection. Their security service took charge of me at the border, their police. I was returned to the border in the same way and I had absolutely no problems. Naturally I didn't go to Belgrade in my own vehicle. I didn't go to the trial in Belgrade in my own vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were you placed in a hotel?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were you able to walk around freely in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had someone who protected me all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: One person?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you walked around freely in the town?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't walk around because I arrived in the evening, I testified in the morning, and I returned immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: My last question was whether you believed that there was a reason for other Croats who were victims in Ovcara, other Croats who saved their lives by chance just like you. You know them some of them, don't mention their names. Do you believe there is any reason for them to ask for protective measures when testifying in this case?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, Mr. Seselj, fear is a subjective matter. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Aren't new witnesses -- someone may feel afraid; others perhaps not. I surrendered my life to God a long time ago so --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But I'm asking you about objective reasons. Are there any objective reasons for such witnesses to be afraid of testifying without having the benefit of protective measures?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, do you know that before your arrival in Vukovar, that while you stayed in Vukovar, a number of crimes were committed against Serbian civilians.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You know nothing.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: As soon as I was told about your name as a protective witness, do you believe me when I say that I first checked to see whether you were on a list of criminals?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe you did everything to discredit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And I can tell you quite frankly that you aren't on the list of criminals that I have, and I will show you the list that I have obtained.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you be so kind as to put this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I wonder what the relevance of this is in this case and whether it can help to clarify certain issues for the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, how will the document you want to show help us? Why is it relevant, useful? And if you have such a document, where was it obtained from? Can you provide us with any information? Because everyone can get hold of a piece of paper and put down the names of alleged criminals without any grounds. So if you have a document, it must be some sort of official document, a document obtained from the police or the judiciary. So could you answer my question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will give you my answers in the order of your questions. You know that my thesis of defence is that the head of the security service of the JNA, General Vasiljevic, ordered the liquidation of Croatian prisoners of war at Ovcara. Another thesis of my defence is that it was not difficult to find the actual perpetrators, the direct perpetrators, and that they were found among frustrated individuals, mostly locals of Vukovar whose closest relatives may have been killed, because the terror over the Serb population of Vukovar lasted for months. So it was not difficult to identify the direct perpetrators. And presenting data on crimes against Serbs is not a way of discrediting this witness. I have no reason to discredit this witness. There's only one statement that I find problematic and that is that he heard my voice on the loudspeaker, a call for surrender. Then later on he adjusted this statement and said that the voice was similar to mine, and there is nothing in his statement that would indict me. But I wish to logically conclude his testimony in an effort to explain the nature of the crimes in Ovcara to show certain facts which indicate that there was a certain number of people among the TO members who had reason for personal revenge, and such individuals among the volunteers could not have existed because their relatives were not living in Vukovar. And if I may be allowed, I would like to show this list which was published by the newspaper Ekspres Politika on the 18th of March, 1997, listing the names of all Croats who took part in the crimes against Serbs, and then I would ask the witness whether he knows two, four, six, eight, ten persons on this list. And if he says yes or no, that would be the end of it. Allow me to put this question to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand well, it's an article in a newspaper dated the 18th of March, 1997, which listed names of Croats who took part in crimes committed against Serbs. That is my understanding.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then I'll show you the official document, too. I have the official document on me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. Before giving you the floor, it's an article in the press, in the public media. What is the objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know what is the relevance and the use of this article, and it has defamatory statements against individuals. I would be a bit embarrassed for us to read such information. Furthermore, the witness is not from Vukovar, he comes from elsewhere, and he is not in my opinion the appropriate person to whom this kind of evidence should be shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, the Prosecutor is making an objection, feeling that this witness is not a good witness for confirming or denying your document. If there are names, they may be people he knows, whether they are Croats who were on the spot in Vukovar, whether they were people who were in Vukovar. If so there's a link; if not there's no link. Can you tell me whether names of Croats on that list are Croats from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am surprised by this question. Why would all of them have to be Croats from Vukovar? Some of them may not be from Vukovar. How should I know? This list was made public, and the heading is "They Committed Crimes against Serbs in Vukovar and the surroundings." I have marked 10 names and I wish to ask the witness whether he knows these people. There is an accompanying text. It doesn't affect the witness in any way. It doesn't affect his credibility. I am satisfied with his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am going to consult my colleagues whether they are for or against. I don't wish to conceal anything. I am for, but if my colleagues are against, they will tell us. In that case it will not be shown. So I am going to consult with my colleagues to see what their position is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have seen the views of my colleagues. They are against, I am for, but they are in a majority so, Mr. Seselj, you cannot use this document. But I would like to add, and I think the Chamber is unanimous in that respect, you will have an opportunity to use this document when you bring your own witnesses to court which will have a direct link to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe even with another of the witnesses of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is for the present the only Prosecution witness for the base-crime -- as a crime-base witness for the crimes in Vukovar, so I have no one else to put this question to, because those coming under 92 ter I will have nothing to do with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's us who will put the question to them in that case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you have another 30 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I expected you to ask questions, as Mrs. Lattanzi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Wait a moment. I'll give her the floor if she wished to intervene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Only to say that I regret Mr. Seselj didn't understand me. I was saying that if a witness comes under 92 ter and there will be relevant questions to put to him, you refuse to cross-examine them, then it will be the Judges who put questions, relevant questions, to those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, concerning the witnesses envisaged for Vukovar, I have numbers that I wish to quote: 2, 4, 9, 12, 14, 16, 30, 34, 35, 36, 39, 40, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46. So there's a whole series of witnesses appearing on the list, so there will certainly be some other viva voce witnesses. So maybe you will have the opportunity to introduce this document. Even if that will not be possible, you will always be able to produce this document through your own witnesses. I was in favour in the spirit of saving time and being effective, but the matter is closed and you still have 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you have not allowed me to question this witness -- to cross-examine this witness about his knowledge about people who committed crimes against Serbian -- against Serbs, I refuse to continue the cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, the accused doesn't wish to ask you any more questions. I have a question, an important question, to put to you which remained in the dark. The Prosecution didn't ask you this. Perhaps Mr. Seselj would have asked you, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You indicated that after you were saved, in a sense, from the carpentry shop you were taken to a civilian prison in Mitrovica, and you said that you were released on the 22nd of May, 1992, within a prisoner exchange. What I would like to know is the following: In Serbia, but that applies to all countries in the world, when someone is put in prison there's a document. People are not put in prison without a document. When you yourself were put in that prison, as far as you know was there a document imprisoning you? Did you meet a lawyer? Did you have an investigating judge talk to you? What happened during the months when you were held in that prison?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first, for the first two months I was in prison without really existing at all. I wasn't registered by the Red Cross or any -- or by any other form or document as proof that I was there. I was registered within the framework of the examinations conducted by -- interrogations by JNA officers, and my name and surname was there, and they even took our photographs. On the 22nd -- 26th of January, 1992, I was registered for the first time through the Red Cross and from then on it was known that I existed as a prisoner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say that you were interrogated by JNA officers. Were they officers belonging to the military police or not?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. I don't know. They wore different uniforms so I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And when you met the Red Cross, did they ask you why you were there?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't ask. There were a lot of us and the reason was known why we were there. I personally was not asked that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it would appear that during these interrogations you were beaten; is that true or false?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What did they want you to say? Did they want to accuse you of crimes? Why were these interrogations conducted?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't my understanding that they wanted to accuse me of a crime. They put standard questions. They were interested in the situation in Vukovar. And several times I didn't know why they hit me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, I should like to take a step back. When you arrived in Vukovar, at the time your country, Croatia, was it an independent country, recognised by the international community, or was it a self-proclaimed independent country? Were you familiar with the exact situation at the time.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croatian assembly proclaimed secession from Yugoslavia and proclaimed its independence. It was internationally recognised by some before the 15th of January, but I know that as of the 15th of January, 1992, it was internationally recognised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. During the battle for Vukovar, Vukovar belonged, in your view, to ex-Yugoslavia or not, or to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an absolutely Croatian town, part of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a Croatian town which belonged to ex-Yugoslavia or to Croatia? I'm referring to November 1991.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a Croatian town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but to an autonomous Croatian state or to an independent state of Croatia, in your view.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about Croatia as an independent state, whose assembly had proclaimed independence. And we know how assembly members are elected by the population's vote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but did you know that the international community did not recognise your country until January 1992.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it did recognise it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but in January 1992.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This, to me, does not seem to be important. I apologise if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When JNA officers interrogated you in the prison, you're telling me that they wanted to know what happened in Vukovar. Were they the only questions they put to you or did they ask you other things as well.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say that, I mean a whole series of questions, starting from, Where do you come from, what were you doing there, what unit did you belong to, where did you fight. This complex set of questions, not just one simple question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking you this because another witness told us that he was charged of rebellion. So these officers, did they accuse you of rebelling against the state, that is, ex-Yugoslavia, or not? Was this part of the questions put to you within the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one accused me, but there was that kind of attitude towards us, that we are rebels, that we are paramilitary troops. That was their position with respect to us. But no one actually charged me with rebellion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're confirming that you didn't see any judge or any military prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least no such person introduced himself as such. I saw officers. Whether they were military prosecutors, military judges, or something else, I don't know. It wasn't their custom to introduce themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'm going to ask my colleagues whether they have any questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Red Cross staff, did they question you about the treatment you were given.

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do have some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe we shall have a break and we can do that after the break. We'll have a 20-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now for the re-examination for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karlovic, page 14 of the transcript is where you answered a question put to you by Mr. Seselj, and you said: [In English] "I don't know who was against us and opposite us in those terms." [Interpretation] You were referring to the enemy. My question is as follows: In Vukovar you had to deal with the JNA, the TO, and the Chetniks; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why are you allowing leading questions of this kind, Mr. President? That's not allowed even in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution is referring to page 14, which is where the witness answered a question that you put to him, so when conducting his re-examination he has the right to refer to your questions and to the answers. He is asking the witness whether in his opinion the JNA, the Chetniks, and the TO were present in Vukovar. He's asking him whether this is correct or not. This is what he could have said, too. The witness said, "Yes, that's correct." So there you have it. I don't see what makes this a leading question. And the Judges also dealt with this question on a number of occasions and the witness said -- or he always answered in the same way. The Prosecution may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Mr. Karlovic, when you were in Vukovar in 1991, did you see any regular JNA soldiers wearing the Chetnik fur cap?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: And during the same period in 1991, when you were in Vukovar, did you see any soldiers, any Chetnik soldiers who -- their hair was cut and it looked like the way JNA soldiers had their hair?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any soldiers like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: In relation to the Territorial Defence, well, how were they dressed usually? Was it like the JNA or were they dressed like the Chetniks? What did they usually look like? How were they usually dressed?

utterances.speaker: VILLEM KARLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was very similar to the regular JNA soldiers, except for the fact that it had Serb flags.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUTERTRE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you have added something that appears for the first time here. The Prosecution asked you whether you made a distinction between JNA soldiers and members of the Territorial Defence and you said they resembled each other, but you added that this wasn't the case for the flags. The Territorial Defence had flags; the JNA had its own flag. Try and explain this flag issue for us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm speaking on the basis of what I know and my opinion and awareness. The territorials used as an insignia the Serb flag, and they had a uniform that was fairly similar to that of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But they had a Serbian flag when engaged in combat? Because when you were arrested, apart from the flag that we saw, we didn't see any others. You're telling us what you know about, but did you find out about this subsequently or was it in Vukovar that you saw such flags?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw both Serb flags and Yugoslav flags. That's what I saw when I was captured, especially when we passed through certain parts of town where they moved around and where they were celebrating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What's good about putting questions is that one always find out new information. So here we have a new flag appearing. Who had Yugoslav flags?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I mostly saw that flag on the APCs and tanks, while the Serb flags were ones that they carried with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
